label: rem:frobenius-codim-universal-interpretation
title: Physical content: the tower residual as $\tau(C_{\dim_q})$
html:
Physical content. Any vortex on the self-dual Frobenius algebra inherits a tower residual. The residual equals the trace of the quantum-co-dimension element scaled by the electron mass m_e:

  \Delta m_{\text{vortex}}
  \;=\;
  m_e \cdot \tau\bigl(C_{\dim_q}^{(A)}\bigr).

Whether a proton tower residual equals this quantity is the comparison recorded in proton tower residual vs m_e\sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q\lambda; no derivation of the residual is claimed. The quantity is not the Markov trace of the Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q) (Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q)).

What the theorem does and does not supply. The identity is a consequence of semisimplicity, not an independent constraint. The element C_{\dim_q} is constructed so that its trace is \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda); once the central idempotents p_\lambda exist with \tau(p_\lambda) and \dim_q(\lambda) invertible, linearity of \tau over that basis gives the identity with nothing further to check. The word universal in the title records that the argument uses no property of A beyond being a semisimple Frobenius algebra with a trace — it does not record a discovery about A.

The content therefore sits in the hypothesis rather than the conclusion. What is being asserted about a quantum universe is that its substrate has channels at all: the Wedderburn semisimplicity axiom supplies the finite block set, the non-vanishing Frobenius weights, and the invertible quantum dimensions. Given those, the co-Casimir trace follows. Read the other way round — as though the numerical identity constrained the algebra — it would be circular.
